key_highlights: ASX treading water as interest rate fears dominate; Wall Street surge offers limited spillover (#10, #32)
Iron ore downside persists, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX near-term (#39)
WA/SA gold exploration surge: Platina, Broken Hill, Forrestania, Great Southern all report positive results (#27, #28, #34, #37)
Sydney housing market in 'bloodbath' with auction reality check; broader affordability crisis (#40, #66)
Super contributions surge >33% post-budget tax changes; new digital pension scheme proposed (#63, #68)
Diesel/petrol price shock rising, pressuring transport and consumer margins (#42)
China economic cracks under Xi raise commodity demand and AUD risks (#24)
Higher interest rates framed as 'new normal', weighing on REITs and growth equities (#44)

sectors.trend: Iron ore weakness persists (#39) but gold exploration is a standout: multiple WA/SA drill results (10.72 g/t Great Southern, Broken Hill sulphide upgrade, Forrestania ground bolt-on, Platina reshuffle) signal a gold rotation. Dalaroo's Greenland rare-earth breakthrough adds critical-minerals upside (#29).
sectors.implications: Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX, WES.AX) and explorers (BHG.AX, FRT.AX, PLT.AX) attract speculative flows. Iron ore majors (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) face margin pressure on China demand doubts. Rare-earths (LRE.AX, DLR.AX) gain strategic relevance.

sectors.trend: Higher-for-longer rate environment supports NIMs but housing stress (Sydney bloodbath, #40) raises credit-risk concerns. Super contribution surge (+33%, #63) and proposed digital pension scheme (#68) expand AUM for fund managers. ASIC action against Super Retail boss signals regulatory tightening (#33).
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from rate tailwind but watch NPL trends. Super fund managers (HUB.AX, PPA.AX) gain from contribution inflows. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) pressured by elevated discount rates.

sectors.trend: Diesel and petrol price shock rising (#42) pressures transport and agribusiness margins. Oil prices falling on Wall Street session (#10) offers partial relief. Victoria's data-centre strategy with renewables mandates (#8) supports renewable-energy and infrastructure names.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX face input-cost pressure. Renewable/infra names (INC.AX, GPT.AX, CGW.AX) benefit from Victoria policy. LNG exporters (WDS.AX, BRL.AX) insulated from domestic fuel shock.

sectors.trend: Wet winter elevates hayfever risk in Victoria (#4), supporting CSL.AX (respiratory therapeutics) and pharmacy chains. Younger Australians face tough economic outlook (#12); burger chain cancels breakfast at hundreds of outlets (#30) signals consumer pullback.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, WES.AX, WES.AX (Woolworths) face mixed signals. Defensive consumer staples preferred over discretionary. Health insurers (IAG.AX, MCF.AX) monitor claims trends.

sectors.trend: Australia joins global AI regulation push (#21); China reshaping AI advisory landscape (#50). Victoria data-centre strategy (#8) drives domestic capex. Ultra-cheap smart glasses hackability (#15) raises cybersecurity concerns.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (W1.AX, XRO.AX, SPL.AX) benefit from data-centre buildout. AI regulation may slow but legitimise sector. Cybersecurity spend rises.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound (5,200–5,500 ^AORD) as rate fears offset Wall Street strength. Gold and banks outperform; iron ore and REITs lag. Fuel shock adds volatility to transport and consumer names. Key watch: RBA commentary and any surprise CPI print.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural shift toward 'higher-for-longer' normalises lower equity multiples. Gold, critical minerals, and infrastructure benefit from policy tailwinds. Housing correction may extend 6–9 months before stabilisation. Super/pension reform expands domestic savings but introduces policy uncertainty. China deceleration caps commodity upside through 2027.
